newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl aide ready to be "chancellor in wheelchair".
newsitem.headline: Kohl aide ready to be "chancellor in wheelchair".

text.p: Wolfgang Schaeuble, the disabled heir apparent to Chancellor Helmut Kohl, said in an interview published on Wednesday he saw no problem in governing Germany from a wheelchair if he ever took over the top job.
Schaeuble, 54, told Stern magazine he was tempted by the position but was not a rival to Kohl and was sure the veteran chancellor would run for reelection in 1998.

The interview left Bonn politicians wondering about the Christian Democratic (CDU) parliamentary leader's plans. Until now he has always loyally avoided any discussion of the succession issue in public.
Schaeuble has been paralysed and confined to a wheelchair since 1990, when he was shot in the jaw and back by a mentally ill man shortly after speaking at a political rally.
"I know I could actually do any job," said Schaeuble, who served as Kohl's chancellery minister and then interior minister before becoming parliamentary leader in 1991.
He admitted the chancellor's job would be tempting if offered and added: "I would probably not resist the temptation."
But he also stressed: "Helmut Kohl knows I would never dump on him."
Schaeuble, a sharp-tongued debater and strong leader, said it was legitimate for voters to ask whether his disability would inhibit him in such a gruelling job.
"Questions about a chancellor in a wheelchair don't bother me," he said. "Helmut Kohl thinks I can do it."
He said he was interested in progress being made in treating spinal cord injuries, like his paralysis, but no longer thinks it could come early enough to help him.
"One cannot defeat the wheelchair," said Schaeuble, who used to ski and play tennis regularly.
